<!-- PROTOTYPE (#15) generated variants: end -->

A handful of words recur throughout this manual. The terms are listed **alphabetically**, so skim the names
and expand any you don't recognise. Nothing here needs to be read end to end;
keep it open and look terms up while following this guide.

<details id="batch">
<summary>**Batch**</summary>

A processing run within a [project](#project) where you ingest your
[metadata workbook](#metadata-workbook) and curate the records through SlideTap.
A project can contain multiple batches — for example if your metadata arrives in
parts — though a single batch is usually enough.

→ You create and complete a batch in [**H. Run a submission**](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details id="bundle">
<summary>**Bundle**</summary>

The `DATASET_<alias>` folder that is the pipeline's finished product — the thing
you validate and upload. It contains `METADATA/` and `IMAGES/`, plus
`LANDING_PAGE/`, `ANNOTATIONS/`, and `PRIVATE/` where used. SlideTap writes it to
the [SlideTap outbox](#slidetap-outbox); from there you validate it and submit it
to BigPicture.

→ You validate the bundle at [**I. Validate**](bp-submission-pipeline/validate.qmd) and upload it at
[**J. Upload to BigPicture**](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details id="coded-attribute">
<summary>**Coded attribute**</summary>

A metadata field whose value is a standardised code (usually
[SNOMED CT](#snomed-ct)) rather than free text — a specimen type or a staining,
for example. Your site's local short codes are translated into coded attributes
by the [mapper workbook](#mapper-workbook). An unmapped value leaves the
attribute empty and makes the item [invalid](#invalid-item).
</details>

<details id="curation-ui">
<summary>**Curation UI**</summary>

The SlideTap web interface where you review and fix your metadata before
submission — mapping values, catching [invalid items](#invalid-item), and
correcting them in the browser. The bp-submission-pipeline path and the Direct
components path both run it; only the Direct upload (sda-cli) path skips it.
</details>

<details id="dataset">
<summary>**Dataset**</summary>

The named entity within your [project](#project) that becomes the dataset record
in BigPicture. This is where you define secondary information: the policy, the
metadata standard version, the type of dataset, and so on. The dataset's
identifier (short name / alias) becomes the folder name of your
[bundle](#bundle) and [outbox](#slidetap-outbox).

→ You configure the dataset in [**H. Run a submission**](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details id="dicomize">
<summary>**DICOMize (pre- and post-process)**</summary>

Converting whole-slide images into the DICOM format BigPicture requires. In the
curation UI this is the **Pre-process** step (download and DICOMize the slides)
followed by **Post-process** (finalise them into the export). Most of a real
submission's time is spent here.

→ Steps 5–6 of [**H. Run a submission**](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details id="encryption-upload-tools">
<summary>**Encryption & upload tools (crypt4gh, sda-cli, bp-submitter)**</summary>

The tools that encrypt the [bundle](#bundle) and send it to BigPicture's inbox.
`crypt4gh` is the encryption format (encrypted files end in `.c4gh`);
`bp-submitter` (used by the pipeline's `make upload`) and `sda-cli` (the manual
Direct upload path) are two alternative uploaders for the same job.

→ [**J. Upload to BigPicture**](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details id="invalid-item">
<summary>**Invalid item**</summary>

A record whose attribute a [mapper](#mapper-workbook) could not resolve — the
value stays `None`, the SlideTap validator flags it, and it blocks export until
fixed. The operator's original input isn't lost: add the missing mapping row,
re-upload `mappers.xlsx`, and re-map from the [curation UI](#curation-ui).
Whole-slide images always show invalid until [pre-processing](#dicomize).

→ Step 4 of [**H. Run a submission**](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details id="landing-page">
<summary>**Landing page**</summary>

The `LANDING_PAGE/` folder and its thumbnails, which appear **publicly** in
BigPicture's Discovery browser. SlideTap does not populate it — you choose
representative, non-sensitive images by hand. `landing_page.xml` is optional at
submission time and can be added later.

→ Step 10 of [**H. Run a submission**](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd), and
[**Add a landing page after submission**](add-landing-page.qmd).
</details>

<details id="mapper-group">
<summary>**Mapper group**</summary>

The named set of mappings a [project](#project) uses, keyed by your institution's
short name (`XLSX_MAPPER_GROUP_NAME`, e.g. `karolinska`). You select it in
Project Settings so the project resolves values against your
[mapper workbook](#mapper-workbook).

→ Step 2 of [**H. Run a submission**](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details id="mapper-workbook">
<summary>**Mapper workbook (`mappers.xlsx`)**</summary>

A spreadsheet you fill in for your site that translates your institution's local
short codes (staining names, tissue types, preparation methods, …) into the
[coded attributes](#coded-attribute) BigPicture expects. Each site maintains its
own mapper workbook.

→ You prepare and provide this at [**E. Reference data**](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data.qmd).
</details>

<details id="metadata-workbook">
<summary>**Metadata workbook**</summary>

The Excel file you create for each submission. It contains the contextual
metadata for your dataset — specimens, observations, whole-slide images, and
their relationships. This is your data: the pipeline ingests it and uses it to
build the submission. (Distinct from the [mapper workbook](#mapper-workbook),
which is reference data you set up once.)

→ You upload this in [**H. Run a submission**](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details id="metaflex">
<summary>**MetaFlex**</summary>

BigPicture's metadata schema — the set of XSD files your exported metadata XML is
validated against. A [bundle](#bundle) whose XML doesn't conform fails
validation. The metadata standard version you pick in the UI (for example
`2.0.0`) selects which MetaFlex schema applies.

→ [**I. Validate**](bp-submission-pipeline/validate.qmd), and
[**Validate metadata**](direct-upload/validate-metadata.qmd) on the Direct upload
path.
</details>

<details id="model-json">
<summary>**model.json**</summary>

A file that describes the structure of a BigPicture-compatible dataset: what
types of data it can contain (specimens, observations, images), how they relate,
and your site's attribute extensions. For most sites the provided default works
unchanged.

→ You supply this file at [**E. Reference data**](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data.qmd).
</details>

<details id="msmdad">
<summary>**MSMDAD**</summary>

BigPicture's **mandatory minimum attribute set** — the floor of attributes every
submission must carry. You get the *entity* floor (case, specimen, block,
slide, image, …) automatically, even from an empty `{}`
[model.json](#model-json). There is **no equivalent built-in floor for
observations**: any MSMDAD attribute that lives inside an observation — a
diagnosis code is the normal case — must still be declared in `model.json`
by hand, or its mapper fails silently at boot and every item using it comes
up unmapped. An observation missing a required MSMDAD attribute fails
export. See [E1. model.json](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-model.qmd) for the full picture.
</details>

<details id="project">
<summary>**Project**</summary>

A container you create in the [curation UI](#curation-ui) that holds everything
for one upload attempt — its [dataset](#dataset) definition and one or more
[batches](#batch). Think of a project as "one dataset going through the
pipeline."

→ You create a project in [**H. Run a submission**](bp-submission-pipeline/run-submission.qmd).
</details>

<details id="reference-data">
<summary>**Reference data**</summary>

The two files the [curation UI](#curation-ui) reads to understand your site:
[model.json](#model-json) (the attribute and observation model) and
[mappers.xlsx](#mapper-workbook) (local codes → coded attributes). You set them
up once, not per submission.

→ [**E. Reference data**](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data.qmd).
</details>

<details id="slidetap-outbox">
<summary>**SlideTap outbox**</summary>

The folder SlideTap writes when a batch finishes its export, named
`DATASET_<your dataset identifier>`. This is the pipeline's direct output — the
[bundle](#bundle) you then validate and upload.

→ You validate the outbox at [**I. Validate**](bp-submission-pipeline/validate.qmd) and upload it at
[**J. Upload to BigPicture**](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd).
</details>

<details id="snomed-ct">
<summary>**SNOMED CT**</summary>

The international clinical terminology whose Concept IDs BigPicture uses for
[coded attributes](#coded-attribute) such as staining procedures and specimen
types. You look codes up in the SNOMED CT Browser and record them in your
[mapper workbook](#mapper-workbook).

→ [**Staining mapping**](bp-submission-pipeline/reference-data-staining.qmd).
</details>

<details id="staging-vs-production">
<summary>**Staging vs production**</summary>

BigPicture runs two upload targets. **Staging** is the test environment the A–J
manual uploads to (`staging-login.bp.nbis.se`, no Terms-of-Use form).
**Production** is the real one (`login.bp.nbis.se`, signed ToU required), with
its own separate credentials. `make upload` requires you to name the `TARGET`.

→ [**J. Upload to BigPicture**](bp-submission-pipeline/upload.qmd), and
[**Prepare for production**](bp-submission-pipeline/prepare-for-production.qmd).
</details>

<details id="wsi">
<summary>**WSI (whole-slide image)**</summary>

A digitised microscopy slide — the image data at the heart of a submission. WSIs
run to gigabytes each and are [DICOMized](#dicomize) during pre-processing; a
real dataset can be terabytes of them.

→ [**Best Practices**](bp-submission-pipeline/best-practices.qmd) for handling large datasets.
</details>
